newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Selling on Outboard "takeunder".
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Selling on Outboard "takeunder".

text.p: Investors were selling stock and options in Outboard Marine Corp Wednesday after a "takeunder" by Detroit Diesel Corp, traders said.

Detriot Diesel said it would acquire Outboard Marine, the largest U.S. maker of outboard engines, for $16 a share in a two-step transaction valued at $500 million that includes $180 million in debt assumption.
Outboard shares ended at 19-1/2 on Tuesday, after bottoming at 10-5/8 in late April. By midday Wednesday the stock was trading at 15-7/8, down 3-5/8, on 1.01 million shares in consolidated activity.
"It's a takeunder," said a market maker in Outboard Marine options, referring to a situation in which a company is bought for less than its current share price.
Last week, some options traders noted that out-of-the-money call buying in July had increased notably, suggesting to some that investors were expecting the company would be acquired.
In April, Outboard Marine said it hired Salomon Brothers to help it explore strategic alternatives. Last week it said it expected an announcement in July.
"There's been a lot of speculation over the last couple of months, but especially over the last few weeks" that the company would be bought, the market maker said.
He said volatilities in the July options had risen sharply on the takeover speculation.
"The July and August got expensive and now there's nothing left in them," he said. "There's definitely a lot more sellers than buyers."
The July 15 call, which traded 230 contracts, dropped 3-1/2 to 7/8 and the July 17-1/2 call, which traded nearly 200 contracts, fell 2-7/16 to 1/16.
"There's a little more play in the August and September options than December just because the deal is not supposed to be finished until October," the market maker said.
The September 15 call was the most active Outboard Marine option with turnover of 610 contracts. It lost 3-3/8 to 1-3/8. The August 15 call traded 315 contracts and fell 3-7/16 to 1-3/16.
The busiest Outboard Marine put was the July 15 with turnover of 225 contracts. It slipped 3/16 to 1/16.
Shares of Detroit Diesel, a unit of closely held Penske Corp, rose 2-1/4 to 26. No options are listed on the stock.
The Ouboard Marine options market maker said Detriot Diesel "is probably getting a steal because if you look historically, this is the low end of Outboard Marine" stock.
